simple.meaning: אֲבִידָע (ʼĂbîydâʻ) is a Hebrew word meaning “Abida , a son of Abraham by Keturah.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲבִידָע (H28) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 25:4, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲבִידָע (H28) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲבִידָע (H28) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲבִידָע (ʼĂbîydâʻ) / H28 is traced through Genesis 25:4, 1 Chronicles 1:33 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Abida , a son of Abraham by Keturah
definitions.full: H28. Abida אֲבִידָע proper name, masculine ( my father took knowledge ) a son of Midian Gen 25:4 ; 1Chr 1:33 . compare Sabean אבידע , Hal MA 192, 202 , also ידעאב , DHM ZMG '83, 399 .
definitions.rootNote: from 1 and 3045 ; father of knowledge (i.e. knowing);

occurrences.englishText: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
